Validation on eth0/channel 0x01 shows the patch works before restart: setting IPFamilyEnables to IPv4Only succeeds, Get LAN returns 11 00, and IPv6AcceptRA/DHCP6 become false. However, after restarting phosphor-ipmi-host.service, Get LAN returns 11 02 (DualStack) while IPv6AcceptRA/DHCP6 remain false on the interface. This indicates a post-restart reporting mismatch (volatile state reset) and Get LAN is not reflecting effective runtime configuration after service restart.

Note: Please correct me if my understanding is wrong? Thanks.

Thanks for the analysis.
 
I initially attempted to model IPv6 disabled state using the existing `DHCP6` and `IPv6AcceptRA` properties. However, those properties only control automatic IPv6 behavior. They can both be disabled in a valid static IPv6 configuration, so they cannot reliably indicate whether IPv6 itself is disabled.
 
To distinguish static IPv6 from fully disabled IPv6, I added an internal map, but the state is local to `phosphor-ipmi-host` and would not persist after a restart.
 
I am now planning to add a separate `IPv6Enabled` property under the network interface object. This property would be the source of truth for whether IPv6 is enabled on the interface. When `IPv6Enabled` is false, the implementation would use the existing `DHCP6` and `IPv6AcceptRA` flags as part of disabling automatic IPv6 behavior, prevent new static IPv6 configuration from becoming active, and persist this state so IPv6 does not return after a reboot.
 
This is the approach I am trying to take. I'm unresolving this to get your inputs so please let me know whether this is feasible, or if there is a better way to model IPv6 disabled state.
Your proposal looks good and ensure it covers persistence, restart/reboot consistency, and static IPv6 behavior validation.
